name: Ceiling & Partition
tagline: The fifth wall, and the walls that are not structural
description: False ceilings hide the services and carry the lighting design; partitions divide space without touching the structure. Both are specified by system — board, framing, fixing and access — not just by finish.

materials.name: Gypsum board
materials.blurb: The standard 12.5 mm board for ceilings and drywall
materials.description: Plaster core in a paper facing, screwed to a GI framework and jointed with tape and compound. Fast, flat and paint-ready — and easily damaged by a roof leak, so keep it out of wet zones.

materials.name: Moisture-resistant gypsum
materials.blurb: Green board for bathrooms, kitchens and balcony soffits
materials.description: Silicone-treated core and water-repellent facing let gypsum survive humid rooms. It is moisture-resistant, not waterproof — a dripping pipe will still finish it.

materials.name: False ceiling (plain gypsum)
materials.blurb: Flat suspended ceiling with concealed services and cove lighting
materials.description: The workhorse residential ceiling: a level plane at 200–450 mm below slab, hiding ducts and wiring and carrying the lighting layout. Always plan access panels for valves and dampers.

materials.name: Metal ceiling
materials.blurb: Powder-coated steel or aluminium panels — demountable and tough
materials.description: Plank, tile or clip-in metal ceilings that hose down and lift out for service access. Standard in airports, hospitals and commercial washrooms.

materials.name: Grid ceiling
materials.blurb: 600×600 lay-in tiles on an exposed T-grid
materials.description: The cheapest fully accessible ceiling: mineral fibre tiles dropped into a visible grid, liftable anywhere for service work. Ubiquitous in offices for exactly that reason.

materials.name: Acoustic ceiling
materials.blurb: Perforated or mineral tiles that absorb reverberation
materials.description: Rated by NRC — how much sound the ceiling soaks up. Essential in open-plan offices, classrooms and restaurants where a hard ceiling turns conversation into noise.

materials.name: PVC ceiling
materials.blurb: Interlocking plastic planks for wet and budget areas
materials.description: Waterproof, cheap and installed in a day over a light frame. Reads as plastic under any decent light, so it belongs in utility rooms rather than living spaces.

materials.name: Wooden ceiling
materials.blurb: Timber planks or veneered panels overhead
materials.description: Real or veneered timber on the ceiling adds warmth nothing else matches — used over dining tables, in entrance lobbies and on balcony soffits. Watch the weight and the fire rating.

materials.name: Baffle ceiling
materials.blurb: Vertical fins hung on edge — rhythm plus acoustics
materials.description: Timber, metal or felt baffles suspended at intervals let services stay visible while adding a strong linear rhythm and real absorption. A favourite in offices and restaurants.

materials.name: Linear ceiling
materials.blurb: Continuous strip panels that stretch a space visually
materials.description: Long aluminium or timber strips with open or closed joints, drawing the eye down a corridor. Also a practical way to integrate linear lighting and slot diffusers.

materials.name: Glass partition
materials.blurb: Framed or frameless glazed divider that keeps the light
materials.description: Splits a plan without darkening it — the standard for cabins, home offices and meeting rooms. Use toughened or laminated glass and add manifestation so nobody walks into it.

materials.name: Gypsum partition
materials.blurb: Drywall stud wall — fast, light, service-friendly
materials.description: A GI stud frame boarded both sides, with insulation and services inside. A quarter the weight of blockwork and up there is a fire and acoustic rating for almost any requirement.

materials.name: Aluminium partition
materials.blurb: Framed modular system for offices and cabins
materials.description: Powder-coated aluminium frames infilled with glass, board or louvres, assembled and dismantled without wet trades. The default when a tenant may reconfigure the floor later.
